headline: High: xonsh can write and egress by default, while ai-engineering-hub has no runtime isolation or verified controls, creating dangerous pairwise misuse and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is tagged for agents/LLMs/MCP/RAG, so it may emit instruction-like content; xonsh reads stdin/stdout and filesystem contents, making a default parsing bridge plausible. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub outputs text that xonsh parses as shell input or instructions
IF the two agents are connected through copied files or piped stdout/stdin
mitigations: Require explicit human review before xonsh executes any text produced by ai-engineering-hub
Wrap ai-engineering-hub outputs in a non-executable format such as JSON with schema validation
Disable automatic piping between the agents
Use a separate staging file for review before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables and has broad network egress, while ai-engineering-hub has no documented runtime isolation or data-handling limits. The pair can therefore move local data into networked outputs in default use, though the exact shared workspace is not documented.
conditions: IF xonsh is run in a workspace containing sensitive files or environment variables
IF xonsh forwards those contents into networked requests or generated outputs
mitigations: Run xonsh in a scrubbed workspace with no secrets present
Unset sensitive environment variables before launch
Block outbound network access for xonsh during paired runs
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs free of raw file contents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh has write_filesystem and execute_shell, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent-oriented repo with no verified concurrency controls. Even without modify_git_state, overlapping writes to the same directory can corrupt artifacts or overwrite outputs; uncertainty about the shared workspace means medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or notebook workspace
IF one agent overwrites files the other is reading or generating
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
Make xonsh operate read-only except for a scratch directory
Snapshot the workspace before paired execution

D_cascading_error.rationale: ai-engineering-hub can produce agentic guidance, and xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If xonsh treats ai-engineering-hub output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. The profiles do not prove this default trust chain, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands derived from ai-engineering-hub output without verification
IF ai-engineering-hub emits incorrect or stale operational instructions
mitigations: Require a verification step before execution
Constrain xonsh to a dry-run mode for agent-produced commands
Log and diff proposed commands against policy
Use allowlisted command templates only

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source docs-only profiles. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, only a low residual risk remains; the other agent is not separately cited beyond its lack of documented compliance constraints.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into xonsh workflows
IF local handling policies require controls not documented in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in paired runs
Document retention and deletion procedures
Review upstream licenses and hosting terms
Keep audit logs of data movement
